Submitted. Summary of the search:

**Final specification:** Equal-weight long feature 30, short feature 3, short feature 27 — in-sample annualized Sharpe (net of costs) = **0.5189**.

**Process:**
1. Declared three stopping rules: stop if best Sharpe > 1.2, stop if failures ≥ 3, restart if last gain ≤ some threshold (later loosened once I recognized it was triggering on ordinary negative-gain exploration rather than genuine staleness).
2. Set a neutral prior (feature 1+) since I had no economically grounded reason to favor any specific feature in this synthetic panel.
3. `init` → anchored on feature 3− (Sharpe 0.38); `extend_best` twice built [3−, 11+, 34+] at 0.5127.
4. The tight `last_gain` restart rule fired after a confirmatory `refine` (which naturally yields ~0 gain), forcing several restarts — I adjusted the trigger once results showed it was mis-calibrated for distinguishing exploration from staleness, logging this as a non-replayable change.
5. Used `pick` among features {3, 11, 34} by `sharpe` (the right statistic for ranking standalone predictive strength when choosing a component) — it selected 3− over my expectation of 11+, correctly reflecting 3−'s higher standalone Sharpe (0.74 vs 0.14).
6. Eventually found an improved branch [30+, 3−, 27−] at 0.5189 via `extend_best`; `refine` confirmed signs were already optimal; `swap_worst` oscillated to a worse point and back, confirming this is a genuine local optimum.
7. Stopped when `failures_at_least(3)` fired, honoring the declared rule rather than continuing to search a plateau.

**OOS prediction:** mean 0.25, sd 0.30 — a substantial haircut from the in-sample 0.52, reflecting selection bias from the iterative search (many candidates scanned per move, multiple restarts) and wide genuine uncertainty about regime stability.
